findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean:36-43 — `variable {F : Type*} [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [FunLike F R S] (f : F) … def map (I : Ideal R) : Ideal S`.
findings.fix: Drop `.toRingHom` from the statement (state it for the `AlgHom` directly) and add `@[simp]`.
findings.issue: `map_connectedComponentIdeal_antipodeAlgHom` is stated as `Ideal.map (HopfAlgebra.antipodeAlgHom k H).toRingHom …`. `Ideal.map` is generalized over `[FunLike F R S]`, so the natural downstream spelling is `Ideal.map (HopfAlgebra.antipodeAlgHom k H) …`; that term has a different `F` argument and FunLike instance, so `rw`/`simp` with this lemma fails against it. The lemma also carries no `@[simp]` despite being a normal-form equation `Ideal.map S I = I`.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn IsNoetherianRing code/TauCeti` yields only this `local instance` and the in-proof `let _` at FiniteType/ConnectedComponents.lean:47; `Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing` is a theorem, not an instance, in Mathlib (used via `have` at mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Jacobson/Artinian.lean:51). `connectedComponentIdempotent`/`connectedComponentIdeal` sit under `variable [LocallyConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R)]` (RingTheory/Idempotents/Connected/Component.lean:75).
findings.fix: Declare a genuine `instance isNoetherianRing (H : FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat R) [IsNoetherianRing R] : IsNoetherianRing H := Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing R H` in `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/FiniteType/CommHopfAlgCat.lean`, delete the `local instance` here, and drop the `let _` at `FiniteType/ConnectedComponents.lean:47`.
findings.issue: `local instance : IsNoetherianRing H` supplies the `LocallyConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum H)` instance that `PrimeSpectrum.connectedComponentIdeal` requires, but no global `IsNoetherianRing ↥H` instance exists for `FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat`. Every consumer of the three exported theorems must re-introduce `Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing k H` by hand before it can even state `connectedComponentIdeal (augmentationPoint k H)`.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Convolution.lean:145-146 `instance convGroup : Group (WithConv <| A →ₐ[R] C)` under `[CommSemiring A] [CommSemiring C] [Bialgebra R C] [HopfAlgebra R A]`; grep for `antipode R (antipode R a)` in mathlib hits only `IsGroupLikeElem.antipode_antipode` (HopfAlgebra/GroupLike.lean:55), and grep for `antipode` in code/TauCeti finds no involutivity lemma outside this file.
findings.fix: State them publicly and in full generality (`{R A} [CommSemiring R] [CommRing A] [HopfAlgebra R A]`) in a general Hopf-algebra file such as `TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/Antipode.lean` — `@[simp] antipode_antipode` plus the `AlgEquiv` — and use the general versions here.
findings.issue: `antipode_involutive` and `antipodeAlgEquiv` are general results — Mathlib's `AlgHom.convGroup` holds for any `[CommSemiring A] [HopfAlgebra R A]` — but they are `private` and needlessly narrowed to a finite-type bundled Hopf algebra over a field. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has them, so the next Layer 3 PR must re-derive them.

The roadmap target it advances is phrased in terms of idempotents, and the component-group step needs the antipode's action on component idempotents.

findings.evidence: Line 170: `· exact antipode_mem_connectedComponentIdeal H` — the mpr direction of the iff is literally the earlier theorem.
findings.fix: Mark `antipode_mem_connectedComponentIdeal` `private` and keep the `@[simp]` iff as the public form; adjust the module docstring's main-declarations list accordingly.
findings.issue: `antipode_mem_connectedComponentIdeal` is exactly `antipode_mem_connectedComponentIdeal_iff.mpr` (line 170 proves the iff's mpr by `exact` on it), so the public surface carries the same fact twice.

summary: The three exported theorems are hard to use downstream: one is stated through an `AlgHom.toRingHom` coercion so it will not rewrite against the natural `Ideal.map (antipodeAlgHom …)` spelling, and all of them depend on a `local instance` that no consumer can reconstruct by typeclass search. The file also hides a general, reusable antipode-involutivity/equivalence pair and its own strongest lemma while exporting a redundant one-directional corollary.
